summary: @servicetitan/eslint-plugin-folder-schema 38.1.7 ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: Version 38.1.7 of this ESLint plugin adds a `preinstall: node setup.mjs` lifecycle hook and two root-level files (setup.mjs, math_init.js) that are not declared in the package's own `files` manifest (which lists only dist/ and src/). On `npm install`, setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases (github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases), extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against the sibling math_init.js via execFileSync. math_init.js is a ~727 KB single-line heavily-obfuscated Bun bundle using rotated string-array obfuscation (WV8StW shift-rotator over the n7gIxM array) with hex-encoded identifiers. Fetching an alternate runtime specifically to execute a bundled obfuscated payload has no legitimate purpose in an ESLint plugin, and running the payload under Bun rather than Node bypasses Node-based supply-chain scanners. The src/ tree still contains the legitimate ESLint rule and the main entry dist/index.js is unchanged, consistent with a hijacked release that appended a dropper to an otherwise legitimate package. The manifest/tarball mismatch (setup.mjs and math_init.js are outside the declared files whitelist) corroborates the smuggling shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
